A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CD45 density is a helpful diagnostic tool in B-CLL and B-PLL, and that it is a useful marker in the differential diagnosis of B-NHL, B-CLL, and B-PLL.
the CD45 density in peripheral blood lymphocytes is useful for the differential diagnosis of B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphomas and chronic lymphoprolifera- tive disorders (CLD).
the CD45 expression level in B-CLL cells is significantly lower than that in B-NHL cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the density of the CD45 receptor is useful in distinguishing B-cell chronic lymphocytic leukemia (B-CLL) and B-cell small lymphocytic lymphoma (B-SLL) from reactive lymphadenopathies (RLP) and follicular lymphomas (FL).

CD45 density is a useful marker to discriminate B-CLL from B-NHL and to differentiate B-CLL patients into two groups with different clinical course: a high CD45 density group with an indolent disease and a low CD45 density group at higher risk for transformation.
CD45 density on B-cell lymphomas can be a useful tool in the differential diagnosis of B-cell lymphomas.
